claims.statement: In 1877 Tom Allen and George Rooke gave sparring exhibitions throughout England.
claims.excerpt: Tom Allen and George Rooke, who it wili be remembered backed out of a fight with him at Pittsburg about two years ago, have been giving sparring exhibitions throughout the Island

claims.statement: Tom Allen's first exhibition in Birmingham, his home town, drew the largest crowd for such an affair in many years.

claims.statement: At Manchester, Tom Allen knocked George Rooke out of time with a left during a sparring bout with gloves.
claims.excerpt: Tom, planting his right on George's chest, caught him in the neck with hie vicious lett, knocking him out of time

claims.statement: A match between Tom Allen and George Rooke, with £25 forfeit a side, was made in 1877 and Allen forfeited his money rather than fight.
claims.excerpt: and £25 forfeit was put up on each side

claims.statement: George Rooke backed out of a fight with Tom Allen at Pittsburg about two years before 1877.
claims.excerpt: backed out of a fight with him at Pittsburg about two years ago

claims.statement: Tom Allen was matched to box Tompkins Gilbert under the new London rules for £50 a side on October 29, 1877.
claims.excerpt: under the new London rules, for £50 aside, on the 29h of this month

claims.statement: Tom Allen wanted to return to America, thinking his trouble in Kentucky might blow over now that Joe Goss had been freed.
claims.excerpt: thinks that, since Goss bas been liberated, sis troubie in Kentucky may in time blow over

notes: Sparring exhibitions and the Rooke match details are from a friend of Allen's who returned from England.
